## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] A Neurology study comparing the alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay on CSF across 4 European laboratories, with 20 patients with DLB and 10 controls, reports average sensitivity of 78.8% (minimum 55%, maximum 100%) and average specificity of 77.5% (minimum 60%, maximum 100%). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-28) — https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000214614 · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] NINDS describes Lewy body dementia as including dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson’s disease dementia. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/lewy-body-dementia · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] The diagnostic-criteria review uses DLB for dementia before or concurrently with parkinsonism and PDD for dementia in well-established Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6987529/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] The diagnostic-criteria review lists fluctuating cognition, recurrent visual hallucinations, REM sleep behavior disorder and spontaneous parkinsonism as core clinical features of DLB. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6987529/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] The Movement Disorder Society task-force abstract characterizes Parkinson’s disease dementia by impairment in attention, memory, executive and visuospatial functions. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17542011/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] The Movement Disorder Society task-force abstract identifies Lewy body-type degeneration in cerebral cortex and limbic structures as the main pathological correlate of Parkinson’s disease dementia. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17542011/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] The DLB Consortium identifies an increased risk of serious sensitivity reactions to antipsychotics in DLB. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5496518/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] NINDS states that not all people with Parkinson’s disease develop dementia and that predicting who will remains difficult. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/lewy-body-dementia · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The DLB Consortium notes that abundant neocortical neuritic plaques and tangles accompanying Lewy bodies can produce a clinical profile resembling Alzheimer disease rather than typical DLB. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5496518/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The consensus report considers the arbitrary timing cutoff clinically useful; the diagnostic-criteria review calls the 1-year rule operational with no scientific basis. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5496518/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6987529/
- [statement] The DLB Consortium defines dementia interfering with normal social, occupational or daily functioning as essential for DLB diagnosis. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5496518/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] The DLB Consortium describes disproportionate attentional, executive and visual-processing deficits relative to memory and naming as typical of DLB. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5496518/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] The DLB Consortium states that normal dopamine-transporter uptake can occur in autopsy-confirmed DLB. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5496518/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] The DLB Consortium states that biomarkers alone do not establish probable DLB. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5496518/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] The DLB Consortium reports that trial meta-analyses support cholinesterase inhibitors for improving cognition, global function and activities of living in DLB. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5496518/ · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
- [statement] The same Neurology study reports that SAA diagnostic performance varied across laboratories, with fair agreement of results (average κ = 0.246), and its authors state that the findings highlight challenges for reproducibility across protocols. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-28) — https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000214614 · keywords: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson's disease dementia
